edges.description: Reproduces the quantitative arm - reduced megakaryocyte yield and fewer platelets released per megakaryocyte.
edges.limitations: iPSC-derived megakaryocytes mature in culture rather than in a marrow niche, so the yield deficit is measured without the stromal and cytokine context that shapes thrombopoiesis in vivo. The patient line also carries the whole 11q deletion, so only the FLI1+/- line isolates the gene.

edges.description: Provides the in vivo half-life and functionality readout for platelets released by FLI1-deficient megakaryocytes, which cannot be obtained in culture.
edges.limitations: The mouse is not FLI1-deficient and does not model the disease; it is a host for human cells. Platelet survival in a xenogeneic circulation is not equivalent to survival in a patient, so the half-life figure is comparative between arms rather than clinically calibrated.

nodes.description: In FLI1-deficient induced megakaryocytes the physically linked ETS-family factor ETS1 is overexpressed, suggesting FLI1 normally represses ETS1 during megakaryopoiesis. Whether this derepression contributes to the disease phenotype or is an incidental consequence of losing FLI1 has not been established, so it is carried as a PROVISIONAL modifier rather than a step in the causal chain.

nodes.description: FLI1 is an ETS-family transcription factor essential to megakaryocyte differentiation. The pathogenic variants that define this disorder cluster in the conserved ETS DNA-binding domain — p.Arg337Trp and p.Tyr343Cys in the dominant series, p.Arg324Trp homozygously in the recessive family — and were shown directly to abolish FLI1 transcriptional activity rather than merely predicted to.

evidence.snippet: This phenotype was caused by a FLI1 homozygous c.970C>T-point mutation that predicts an arginine-to-tryptophan substitution in the conserved ETS DNA-binding domain of FLI1.

genetic_context.description: Reported alleles are germline missense variants in the ETS DNA-binding domain, plus a frameshift deletion predicting haploinsufficiency. Both heterozygous and homozygous genotypes are reported.

nodes.description: The convergence node shared with the rest of the inherited platelet function disorders. Made explicit so this entry joins the family at the step the mechanism module treats as rate-limiting. Only the qualitative (granule/secretion) arm is routed through this node; the entry's separate thrombopoiesis arm reaches the bleeding phenotype directly, because impaired platelet production is a mechanistically distinct route that the module deliberately does not model.

evidence.reference_title: Advances in our understanding of the molecular basis of disorders of platelet function.
evidence.snippet: Genetic defects of platelet function give rise to mucocutaneous bleeding of varying severity because platelets fail to fulfil their haemostatic role after vessel injury.

nodes.description: With the terminal transcriptional programme disabled, megakaryocyte output falls at two points: fewer megakaryocytes are produced, and each releases fewer platelets. This was shown directly in induced pluripotent stem cell-derived megakaryocytes from a Paris-Trousseau patient and from a targeted heterozygous FLI1 knockout line, which reproduced the described megakaryocyte and platelet features. It is the quantitative arm of the disorder, producing the mild-to-moderate thrombocytopenia.

nodes.description: FLI1 directly transactivates the promoters of platelet genes required for adhesion, aggregation and granule biology — GP6 (the collagen receptor glycoprotein VI), GP9 (part of the von Willebrand factor receptor complex) and ITGA2B (integrin alpha-IIb). The recessive allele was shown to cause a transcription defect at all three promoters by luciferase assay, and, more tellingly, to reduce the corresponding proteins in platelets taken from affected family members. The promoter assay and the patient Western blot are what make this a demonstrated mechanism rather than an inferred one.

evidence.reference_title: Paris-Trousseau thrombocytopenia is phenocopied by the autosomal recessive inheritance of a DNA-binding domain mutation in FLI1.
evidence.snippet: This mutation caused a transcription defect at the promoter of known FLI1 target genes GP6, GP9, and ITGA2B, as measured by luciferase assay in HEK293 cells, and decreased the expression of these target proteins in affected members of the family as measured by Western blotting of platelet lysates.

nodes.description: Reduced platelet number combined with defective platelet function produces excessive mucocutaneous bleeding — the presenting complaint through which these patients are ascertained. Because the defect is qualitative as well as quantitative, bleeding severity is not predicted by the platelet count alone, and thrombocytopenia is characteristically only mild to moderate.

evidence.reference_title: Enrichment of FLI1 and RUNX1 mutations in families with excessive bleeding and platelet dense granule secretion defects.
evidence.snippet: Our findings suggest that alterations in FLI1 and RUNX1 may be common in patients with platelet dense granule secretion defects and mild thrombocytopenia.

nodes.description: A xenotransplantation readout rather than a genetic disease model: NSG mice are infused with human iMegs and the platelets those cells release are tracked. The mouse contributes the circulation, not the lesion.

iPSC-derived megakaryocytes from a Paris-Trousseau patient and from a control line carrying a targeted heterozygous FLI1 knockout. The FLI1+/- line is the one that bears on this entry: it isolates FLI1 haploinsufficiency from the contiguous 11q deletion that confounds Paris-Trousseau.

The qualitative arm. Circulating platelets show a dense granule secretion defect with impaired aggregation to a panel of agonists, and in the recessive family a striking alpha-granule abnormality: large, fused alpha-granules in a minority of platelets, the same morphological hallmark seen in Paris-Trousseau thrombocytopenia. Collagen-induced aggregation was absent in that family, which fits the demonstrated loss of the FLI1 target GP6, the collagen receptor.

evidence.reference_title: Enrichment of FLI1 and RUNX1 mutations in families with excessive bleeding and platelet dense granule secretion defects.
evidence.snippet: We analyzed candidate platelet function disorder genes in 13 index cases with a history of excessive bleeding in association with a significant reduction in dense granule secretion and impaired aggregation to a panel of platelet agonists.

evidence.reference_title: Paris-Trousseau thrombocytopenia is phenocopied by the autosomal recessive inheritance of a DNA-binding domain mutation in FLI1.
evidence.snippet: Affected individuals in this family have moderate thrombocytopenia; absent collagen-induced platelet aggregation; and large, fused α-granules in 1% to 5% of circulating platelets.
